title: Bibliometric and visualized analysis of research trends and knowledge structure in novel pharmacological treatments for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Zhen Chen; Fen Ai; Jinlei Li; Bingxin Cheng; Weihao Cheng; Yu Li
abstract:
This study presents a bibliometric and visual analysis of the literature on novel drug therapies for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) to explore recent research trends, hotspots, and developmental directions.
Publications related to novel drug treatments for HCM from 2015 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. CiteSpace and VOSviewer (with standard parameters: time slicing 2015-2025, node selection based on co-occurrence, and pathfinder pruning) were utilized for quantitative and visual analyses.
After screening, 281 publications were included. The annual publication output exhibited an overall upward trend. The United States led in the number of publications, while England played a prominent hub role in international collaboration. The Harvard University system formed a high-yield cluster, and the University of California system served as a key bridge. Co-citation analysis of journals revealed an interdisciplinary knowledge structure spanning basic science to clinical medicine. Both reference and keyword analyses confirmed that the research frontier has shifted from early exploration of the cardiac myosin mechanism to a current focus on myosin inhibitors.
Bibliometric evidence indicates a clear shift toward targeted therapy centered on cardiac myosin inhibitors, marking a transition in research focus. These findings provide a quantitative roadmap for researchers and clinicians to identify key players, collaborative opportunities, and emerging topics. Future studies are expected to deepen focus on non-obstructive HCM, personalized treatment, and long-term efficacy verification.

title: Inter-American consensus on hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Josefina B Parodi; Cristhian E Scatularo; Enrique A Berríos-Bárcenas; Juan D López-Ponce de León; Diego Pérez de Arenaza; Luis E Gómez; Juan P Costabel; Fabio Fernandes; Clara Saldarriaga; Víctor Rossel; Carlos E Rochitte; Ricardo Stein; Roberto Concepción-Chacón; Gabriel Parma-Romanelli; Karina González-Carta; Susana Blanco-Sobrino; Daniel Sierra-Lara-Martínez; Franco Leoni; Jorge Jalil; Yamiris Delgado; Diego X Chango; Liliana Posada-Martínez; Landy Rodríguez-Amaguay; Carlos Guamán-Valdivieso; Jairo A Rendón-Giraldo; Víctor Arévalos; Ingrid Márquez; Florencia B Cantora; Mariano D Estofán; Ivonne Cárdenas-Reyes; Noël Brögger; María C Bejarano; Joffre Lara-Terán; Ignacio Vaca-Valverde; Carlos Olivares-Asencio; Leandro Cura-Hochbaum; Paola A Morejón-Barragán; Agostina M Fava; Andrés F Miranda-Arboleda; Manlio F Márquez-Murillo; Eric Karabut; Ana C Berni-Betancourt; Ana C Alba; María J Rodríguez-González; María M Sáenz-Tejeira; Katihurca Almonte-Montes de Oca; Rosa N Cueto; Melissa Rodríguez-Israel; Alicia G Torterolo-Herrera; Vicente Villacreses; Gustavo Restrepo; María I Sosa-Liprandi; Eugenio Cingolani; Sergio Baratta; Ricardo López-Santi; Ana Múnera-Echeverri; Adrián Baranchuk
abstract:
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common inherited cardiomyopathy and poses major diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in Latin America, owing to heterogeneity in resource availability, access to advanced technologies, and the organization of health systems.
To develop the first Inter-American Consensus on HCM, in order to standardize the care of these patients tailored to the regional context.
The Inter-American Society of Cardiology (SIAC) convened a committee of experts from different countries across the Americas. A systematic review of the evidence was performed, followed by the development of recommendations, which were validated using a formal Delphi methodology; consensus was defined as agreement among more than 80% of participants.
The consensus provides a comprehensive approach to the evaluation and management of HCM. It covers epidemiology, pathophysiology, multimodality diagnostic tools, genetics and family counseling, phenocopies, pharmacological and invasive treatment, associated complications, sudden cardiac death risk assessment, special populations (pediatric and pregnant patients), physical exercise, and follow-up strategies. In addition, it includes specific recommendations aimed at facilitating the implementation of these across Latin America.
The Inter-American Consensus on HCM provides recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of this condition. It integrates the best available evidence with regional clinical experience and takes into account the epidemiological, economic, and healthcare characteristics of the region. It constitutes a reference framework for standardizing the care of patients with HCM and their families throughout Latin America.

title: Transcriptomics Identifies a Small Set of Circulating Biomarkers and Signaling Pathways Dysregulated in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
authors: Yuko Kiyohara; Keitaro Akita; Michael A Fifer; Albree Tower-Rader; Sergio Teruya; Bilal Ansari; Alfonsina M Santos; Mathew S Maurer; Yuichi J Shimada
abstract:
It is sometimes challenging to distinguish hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) from other cardiomyopathies with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). At present, no circulating biomarkers to distinguish HCM have been established.
The authors aimed to identify plasma microRNA (miRNA) biomarkers unique to HCM.
In this multicenter case-control study, the authors performed comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling in cases with HCM and controls with hypertensive LVH, transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), and aortic stenosis (AS). For each disease group, they chronologically split the patients into training and test sets. The authors identified miRNAs that were significantly (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05) upregulated or downregulated in HCM compared with hypertensive LVH. They made the same comparisons between HCM and ATTR-CM and between HCM and AS. They determined miRNAs that were consistently upregulated or downregulated in HCM throughout all 3 comparisons. Then, they selected miRNAs independently associated with HCM after adjusting for potential confounders. Using the selected miRNAs, the authors developed a logistic regression model to distinguish HCM in the training set. They calculated the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve in the test set.
The authors analyzed 2,656 miRNAs in patients with HCM (n = 294), hypertensive LVH (n = 321), ATTR-CM (n = 167), and AS (n = 38). They identified 3 miRNAs (miR-454-3p, miR-98-5p, and miR-5581-3p). The logistic regression model using the 3 miRNAs had an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.93-0.97) with a sensitivity of 0.95 and a specificity of 0.90 in the test set.
Comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling identified a small set of circulating miRNAs to distinguish HCM from other cardiomyopathies with LVH.

title: Predictors of Early Mortality After Open Aorto-Iliac Reconstruction in Patients with Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: An Observational Cohort Study.
authors: Merei Imanbayev; Altay Dyussupov; Bekzhigit Tussupkanov; Ergali Muratzhanov; Ardak Mautbekova; Dinara Kozubayeva; Rustam Mukhametkhanov; Rail Gafurov; Nurbek Irgebayev; Dainius Pavalkis; Evgeniy Zhuravlev; Yersyn Sabitov
abstract: Background and Objectives: Open aorto-iliac reconstruction (AIR) for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD) remains a high-risk procedure due to multifocal atherosclerosis affecting coronary, cerebrovascular, and renal arterial beds. This study aimed to identify factors independently associated with 30-day mortality and explore factors associated with late mortality during available follow-up among 30-day survivors following open AIR. Materials and Methods: An observational, non-randomised cohort of 170 consecutive patients undergoing open AIR for AIOD between January 2018 and December 2024 was analysed. Univariate logistic regression was performed for 30-day mortality; given the limited number of events (n = 16), the primary multivariable analysis used penalized likelihood logistic regression (Firth correction). Late survival among 30-day survivors (landmark cohort, n = 154) was analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and exploratory univariate Cox proportional hazards regression, with surviving patients censored at the last available follow-up; multivariable Cox modelling was not performed due to the limited number of late events (n = 10). Results: Thirty-day mortality was 9.4% (16/170) in the overall cohort. In the primary Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression, factors associated with 30-day mortality were: severe left IIA stenosis ≥ 70% (OR 9.68; 95% CI 3.08-30.43; p = 0.0001), chronic kidney disease (OR 3.62; 95% CI 1.03-12.66; p = 0.044), and increasing aortic cross-clamp duration, analysed continuously (OR 1.022 per minute; 95% CI 1.000-1.045); a conventional ≥60 min categorical threshold showed a consistent secondary association (OR 4.15; 95% CI 1.28-13.46; p = 0.018). Non-inclusion of IIA was associated with increased 30-day mortality on univariate analysis (OR 4.80; 95% CI 1.31-17.62; p = 0.018). Among the 154 patients entering the 30-day landmark cohort, 10 late deaths were observed during available follow-up. In exploratory univariate Cox regression, intraoperative blood loss was the only statistically significant factor associated with late mortality (HR 1.07 per 100 mL; 95% CI 1.03-1.12; p = 0.0006). Conclusions: Severe IIA disease, chronic kidney disease, and increasing aortic cross-clamp duration (analysed continuously) were independently associated with increased 30-day mortality after open AIR. Intraoperative blood loss was associated with late mortality in exploratory univariate survival analysis. These findings require validation in larger prospective cohorts with longer and more uniform follow-up.

title: Unravelling the Diagnosis of Normal-Flow Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis: The Role of Multimodality Imaging.
authors: Laura Rotondo; Elena Marchetti; Rita Pavasini; Elisabetta Tonet; Carlo Tumscitz; Carlo Penzo; Marta Cocco; Maria Lo Monaco; Erika Bertella; Gianluca Campo; Federico Marchini
abstract: Normal-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis is one of the most deceptive presentations of aortic stenosis. It leaves clinicians uncertain whether they are facing true severe disease or a measurement artefact. This often reflects a discordant grading pattern, in which many patients ultimately prove to have moderate disease. This diagnostic paradox arises from a combination of measurement errors, geometric assumptions, and genuine hemodynamic complexity, and cannot be resolved by echocardiography alone. A structured multimodality imaging strategy integrating calcium score evaluation on cardiac computed tomography, tissue characterisation on cardiac magnetic resonance and, when necessary, invasive hemodynamic assessment is the only reliable path to diagnostic certainty and appropriate therapeutic decision-making. Together, these modalities form a coherent sequential algorithm that moves from the non-invasive to the invasive, from the hemodynamic to the biological, and from uncertainty to actionable clinical decision. This review provides an updated, critical appraisal of each imaging tool and its respective strengths and pitfalls.

title: Documented Valvular Regurgitation and Explicit Heart Failure in an Internal Medicine Registry: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Maria Rada; Maria-Laura Craciun; Ana-Maria Pah; Diana Utu; Dana Emilia Velimirovici; Diana-Maria Mateescu; Ioana Cotet; Ariana Bianca Velciov; Cristiana Adina Avram
abstract: Background and Objectives: Routine records may conflate valvular heart disease (VHD), functional classification, and shared diagnostic assessment. We quantified the cross-sectional association between a registry VHD label and explicitly documented heart failure (HF), while recognizing that every observed valve lesion was regurgitant. Materials and Methods: The analytic sample comprised all 224 eligible adults admitted to the Internal Medicine II Department of a railway-affiliated hospital between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2026: 38 with documented VHD and 186 without documented VHD. The primary outcome was an explicit HF diagnosis; a combined HF/NYHA-positive field was examined as an over-inclusive sensitivity outcome. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking history, and total cholesterol. Results: Explicit HF was documented in 24/38 patients with VHD (63.2%) and 72/186 without VHD (38.7%; adjusted OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.38-5.99). The combined outcome was present in 28/38 (73.7%) and 101/186 (54.3%), respectively (adjusted OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.09-5.21). All 38 exposed patients had documented mitral, aortic, and/or tricuspid regurgitation; no stenosis, prolapse, or prior valve intervention was recorded. Conclusions: Documented valvular regurgitation was associated with explicit HF documentation. Because regurgitation may be secondary to ventricular or atrial disease, reverse causation, shared ascertainment, non-adjudicated diagnoses, and residual confounding preclude causal, temporal, prognostic, or lesion-specific inference.

title: Sutureless Aortic Valve Replacement with the Perceval Plus® Versus TAVI: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Postoperative Outcomes, Hematological Dynamics, and Inflammatory Response.
authors: Umit Kahraman; Irem Demiray; Serkan Ertugay; Emrah Oguz; Oguz Yavuzgil; Hakan Posacioglu; Anıl Ziya Apaydin; Ismet Tanzer Calkavur; Mustafa Ozbaran; Tahir Yagdi
abstract: Perceval Plus and TAVI are increasingly used for severe aortic stenosis, both relying on a self-expanding nitinol stent design, yet evidence specific to Perceval Plus remains limited regarding postoperative clinical outcomes and hematological and inflammatory dynamics. We compared postoperative clinical outcomes and longitudinal platelet/CRP dynamics between Perceval Plus and TAVI in a retrospective single-center cohort, in which 26 propensity score-matched pairs were obtained (1:1 matching) from patients undergoing Su-AVR (Perceval Plus, n = 53) or TAVI (self-expanding Medtronic devices, n = 101). Mortality, echocardiographic outcomes, and rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation and conduction disturbances showed no statistically significant differences between groups, while TAVI was associated with shorter ICU and hospital stay and Su-AVR required higher FFP transfusion (p = 0.016). Platelet count declined in both groups, with a deeper nadir in Su-AVR (postoperative day 3: 66% decline) versus TAVI (day 4: 27% decline), with a significant group × time interaction (p = 0.013); CRP rose in both groups but more rapidly and to a greater magnitude in Su-AVR (time and group × time interaction, both p < 0.001). Su-AVR and TAVI showed no statistically significant differences in the clinical safety outcomes assessed but differed in postoperative hematological and inflammatory magnitude, likely reflecting multifactorial procedure- and device-related mechanisms, warranting confirmation in larger, prospective, multicenter studies.

title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis.
authors: Antonio De Vita; Marcello Covino; Francesco Mollo; Matteo Vumbaca; Chiara Napolitano; Saverio Tremamunno; Nello Cambise; Rosaria Natali; Marco Rossi; Tiziana Bove; Raffaele Vitiello; Giulio Maccauro; Francesco Franceschi; Carlo Trani; Francesco Burzotta; Gaetano Antonio Lanza
abstract: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04-2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03-0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

title: Early and Long-Term Results of 101 Consecutive Patients After Transcarotid Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authors: Damian Hudziak; Monika Gruz-Kwapisz; Radosław Parma; Wojciech Wańha; Sylwia Gładysz-Wańha; Wojciech Wojakowski; Radosław Gocoł
abstract: Background/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation through the common carotid artery (TC-TAVI) is one of the possible treatment options for patients with ineligible transfemoral approach. The aim of our study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of patients treated with TC-TAVI in early and long-term follow-up. Methods: The study included patients with severe aortic stenosis treated with TC-TAVI. In-hospital outcomes, early, long-term follow-up were presented in accordance with the VARC-3 recommendations. Results: The analysis presented 101 patients. We observed high procedural success-97% (n = 98). The number of VARC-3 incidents: 3.96% major vascular complications; 0.99% myocardial infarction; 0.99% cardiac tamponade; 0.99% life-threatening bleeding; 3.96% cerebrovascular incidents. The NYHA class decreased significantly compared to the pre-procedure value (2 [1-2] vs. 3 [3-3]; p < 0.001). There was a significant improvement in postprocedural cerebral oximetry values compared to baseline on both the implanted and contralateral sides (67.5 [63-71]% vs. 70 [63.5-75]%; p < 0.05) and (67 [64-71]% vs. 71 [64-76]%; p < 0.05), respectively. The 30-day, 1-year, and 2-year survival rates were 94.1%, 80.2%, and 69.3%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, BAV (HR 4.54; 95% CI: 1.14-17.99; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 7.32; 95% CI: 2.59-20.65; p < 0.001) were significantly associated with two-year mortality. In an exploratory adjusted Cox regression analysis, BAV (HR 2.63; 95% CI: 1.07-6.45; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 3.48; 95% CI: 1.67-7.24; p < 0.001) were associated with higher 2-year mortality. Conclusions: Our single-center, observational report indicated feasibility and good observed outcomes of the TC-TAVI procedure in an experienced clinical team.

title: Research trends and hotspot analysis of sudden cardiac death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: A bibliometric analysis.
authors: Zhen Chen; Fen Ai; Jinlei Li; Yu Li
abstract:
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common genetic heart disease and a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. This study aims to map the research landscape of Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy -related sudden cardiac death over the past 2 decades using bibliometric methods.
We performed a bibliometric analysis of 712 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (2005-2025). Using Cite Space, we examined publication trends, collaboration networks, co-citation patterns, and keyword dynamics.
Annual publication output rose markedly, with pronounced accelerations after the 2014 European Society of Cardiology and 2020 American heart association/American College of Cardiology guidelines. The United States led in productivity (203 publications) and network centrality (0.40), while China ranked second in output (123 publications) but exhibited limited international collaboration (centrality = 0.01). Co‑citation analysis indicated that clinical guidelines and risk‑prediction models form the field' score knowledge base, and five of the ten most cited references were international guidelines. Keyword analysis defined 4 principal thematic clusters disease entity, clinical outcomes, imaging biomarkers, and risk stratification and documented a shift from early mechanistic studies to multimodal risk prediction, followed more recently by artificial intelligence-driven models and targeted pharmacological therapies (e.g., mavacamten).
This study provides a systematic, data-driven overview of the knowledge structure and evolutionary trends in Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-related sudden Cardiac death research. The findings underscore the field' s guideline-driven character, document the rise of AI-based risk stratification, and describe a paradigm shift toward disease-modifying therapies, offering actionable insights for prioritizing future research and informing clinical decision-making.

title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
authors: Giovanni Baglio; Elena G Bignami; Leonardo De Luca; Elisa Guglielmi; Ciro Indolfi; Alfredo Marchese; Fabrizio Oliva; Ettore Panascia; Gianluca Paternoster; Pasquale Perrone Filardi; Michele Pilato; Marco Ranucci; Mauro Rinaldi; Francesco Saia
abstract: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.

title: Prosthesis-patient mismatch after surgical aortic valve replacement with aortic annular enlargement in small aortic annuli.
authors: Xander Jacquemyn; Mahnoor Imran; Derek Serna-Gallegos; Irsa Hasan; Takuya Ogami; Johannes Bonnati; David J Kaczorowski; Danny Chu; David West; Ibrahim Sultan
abstract:
Aortic annular enlargement (AAE) during surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) is performed to facilitate implantation of larger prostheses in patients with small aortic annuli and mitigate prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). However, the clinical impact of residual PPM after AAE remains uncertain.
All adult patients who underwent SAVR with AAE for small aortic annuli were retrospectively identified from a prospectively maintained institutional database (2011-2024). PPM was defined based on indexed effective orifice area thresholds derived from published reference tables. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and secondary outcomes included heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and longitudinal echocardiographic performance.
A total of 169 patients were identified (age 68 years [61-73], 119 female [70.4%]). Median STS risk was 2% [1-4%], and preoperative mean gradient was 45.0 mmHg [36.8-57.2]. Overall median valve size after AAE was 23 mm (21-25), and PPM occurred in 25 patients (14.8%), including 24 (14.2%) with moderate and 1 (0.6%) with severe PPM. Early outcomes were comparable between PPM and no-PPM groups: postoperative stroke 0 (0%) vs. 3 (2.1%, p > 0.999), and 30-day mortality 1 (4.0%) vs. 5 (3.5%, p > 0.999). Over 4 years follow-up, survival (HR 0.94, 95%CI 0.40-2.21, p = 0.896) and freedom from HF hospitalization (HR 1.16, 95%CI 0.45-2.95, p = 0.760) were similar. Echocardiographic trends showed no differences in LVEF (p = 0.123) or mean gradient (p = 0.879) during follow-up.
In patients with small aortic annuli undergoing SAVR with annular enlargement, the incidence of PPM was low, and residual PPM did not adversely impact early postoperative outcomes, mid-term survival, or valve hemodynamics.

title: Long-term outcomes of congenital subaortic stenosis surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Yusuf Shieba; Juan Olivello; Abdulrahman Asiri; Rashad Zayat; Ajay Moza; Lachmandath Tewarie; Ahmed F A Mohammed
abstract:
To estimate recurrence, reoperation, and aortic insufficiency progression after pediatric surgery for subaortic stenosis and explore associated study-level factors.
PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for eligible studies published from 1 January 2012 to 3 July 2025. We included observational studies of patients <18 years undergoing surgical resection for SAS with a study-level mean or median postoperative follow-up of ≥ 3 years, which was the prespecified operational definition of long-term follow-up. Proportions were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was quantified using I²; meta-regression assessed study-level associations with reoperation and AI progression; and risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.
Seventeen retrospective studies included 1,536 patients; 1,493 contributed to the recurrence analysis. Follow-up ranged from 3.0 to 12.7 years. Overall recurrence was 21% (95% confidence interval, 16-28%; I²=88.1%). Reoperation across 16 studies was 17% (95% confidence interval, 14-20%; I²=41.6%); a prespecified definition-harmonized sensitivity analysis yielded the same estimate (17%; 95% confidence interval, 15-20%; I²=19.1%). In isolated discrete subaortic stenosis, reoperation was 8% and 12% after definition harmonization. Progression to moderate or severe aortic insufficiency was 10% (95% confidence interval, 8-13%). Older study-level age at surgery was inversely associated with reoperation (β = -0.2230; P = 0.0138), whereas higher preoperative peak left ventricular outflow tract gradient was associated with aortic insufficiency progression (odds ratio per 10-mmHg increase, 1.25; P = 0.0072).
Reoperation and clinically important aortic insufficiency remain substantial during follow-up after pediatric subaortic stenosis surgery. Meta-regression findings are exploratory, aggregate associations and should not guide individual operative timing or risk prediction.

title: Trends and Disparities in Aortic Stenosis-Related Mortality Among Adults Aged ≥65 Years in the United States From 1999 to 2024.
authors: Aymen Ahmed; Muteia Shakoor; Usama Hussain Kamal; Hiba Sohail; Muhammad Hasnain Mankani; Vikash Jaiswal; Najam Us Saqib; Nso Nso; Arman Qamar; Mark J Ricciardi
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Aortic stenosis (AS) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular death, yet temporal mortality trends specifically among older adults remain poorly characterized. This study analyzed trends and disparities in AS-related mortality among older adults in the United States from 1999 to 2024.
Using the CDC WONDER database, we analyzed AS-related deaths among adults aged ≥65 years. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMR) and average annual percent change (AAPC) were calculated across demographic and geographic subgroups.
A total of 637,178 deaths were recorded. The overall AAMR for AS-related mortality decreased significantly from 1999 (55.74) to 2024 (52.46) (AAPC, -0.23; P =.004). Although rates rose from 2018 to 2021, a significant decline followed through 2024 (annual percent change, -2.40). Men had consistently higher AAMR than women; mortality remained stable in men (AAPC, -0.06; P = .33), but declined among women (AAPC, -0.35; P =.002). AS-related mortality decreased among patients aged 75 to 84 years, but increased in those ≥85 years (AAPC, 0.28), who had the highest AAMR throughout. Mortality declined in all census regions except for the Midwest, reaching the highest AAMR in 2024 (60.91). Nonmetropolitan areas saw increasing trends, whereas metropolitan areas saw declines. AAMR remained highest among non-Hispanic (NH) White individuals; however, significant decreases were observed in Hispanic/Latino and NH Asian/Pacific Islander populations.
Aortic stenosis-related mortality declined modestly among older adults from 1999 to 2024. However, notable demographic and regional disparities persisted, including higher mortality in men, NH White individuals, older adults ≥85 years, and residents of nonmetropolitan regions and the Midwest. Further investigation and targeted interventions are needed to improve outcomes.

title: Routine Versus Deferred Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Reconstructed Individual Patient Data.
authors: Mahmoud Balata; Ahmed Samy Badran; Mohamed Ibrahim Gbreel; Marwa Hassan; Islam Ebeid; Abdelhakim A Abdelrahman; Daniel Robinson; Jonas Bodanowitz; Stephan Valenta; Christin Valenta; Plamen Kochev; Hüseyin Ince; Jasmin Ortak
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
The optimal management of concomitant coronary artery disease in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains controversial. Whether routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR provides clinical benefit compared to a strategy of deferral is unclear.
We performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCT) comparing routine PCI before TAVR with a strategy of PCI deferral. The primary end points were a composite of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and all-cause mortality. Secondary end points included myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularization, and major bleeding. We applied a random-effects model to calculate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% CI. We also performed a pooled time-to-event analysis using reconstructed individual patient data.
We included 3 RCT (ACTIVATION, NOTION-3, and PRO-TAVI) comprising a total of 1156 patients. The pooled cohort had a median age exceeding 81 years and exhibited low anatomic coronary complexity (median SYNTAX score ≤10). Routine PCI did not significantly reduce the risk of MACCE (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.62-1.13; P = .25) or all-cause mortality (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.67-1.17; P = .38). Pooled Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed no difference in all-cause mortality over 48 months (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.68-1.17; P = .41). Although routine PCI was associated with a significant reduction in any revascularization (HR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.06-0.89; P = .03) and urgent revascularization (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.12-0.87; P = .02), it was associated with increased bleeding events (HR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.28-3.00; P < .01). No significant differences were observed regarding myocardial infarction or stroke.
Routine PCI before TAVR did not reduce mortality or MACCE compared to a deferral strategy. Although routine PCI lowered the risk of subsequent urgent revascularization, it significantly increased the risk of major bleeding.

title: Right internal jugular approach for transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair using the MitraClip G4 system after failed transfemoral access: a case report.
authors: Yutaka Konami; Kazuhisa Kodama; Mika Maeda; Masahiro Yamada; Tomohiro Sakamoto
abstract:
Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair of the mitral valve is conventionally performed via transfemoral venous access. When this route is not feasible, the right internal jugular vein may provide an alternative, but procedural experience remains limited.
A 93-year-old woman with refractory heart failure had atrial functional mitral regurgitation and low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis. After transcatheter aortic valve implantation, moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation persisted. Transfemoral edge-to-edge repair was unsuccessful because severe iliac venous tortuosity prevented adequate catheter control. The procedure was subsequently performed via the right internal jugular vein using the MitraClip G4 system. A pre-existing iatrogenic atrial septal defect was reused, and temporary left ventricular apical wire support facilitated advancement of the steerable guiding catheter into the left atrium. Stepwise + knob rotation increased height and working space, improved the markedly under-straddled configuration, and permitted further advancement of the clip delivery system. Subsequent M- and P-knob adjustments achieved an appropriate trajectory towards A2/P2, with an S-shaped fluoroscopic configuration. Leaflet grasping reduced mitral regurgitation to mild without access-site complications. Mild mitral regurgitation was maintained at 6 months without heart-failure rehospitalization.
Right internal jugular access may be a feasible alternative when transfemoral access is not possible. Successful navigation requires recognition of access-specific catheter behaviour and adaptation of steering under real-time fluoroscopy and transoesophageal echocardiography. An S-shaped fluoroscopic configuration may serve as a practical landmark of a favourable trajectory towards the mitral valve.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Concurrent Impella-Assisted High-Risk PCI and TAVR in Patients With Complex Coronary Artery Disease and Severe Aortic Stenosis.
authors: Frederick Berro Rivera; Brenden Ingraham; Pietro Di Santo; Trevor Simard; Benjamin Hibbert; Mandeep Singh
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Percutaneous management of high risk, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) needing mechanical support for complex coronary artery disease in patients needing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis remains incompletely defined. We report on the feasibility and safety of a single-session strategy using Impella-assisted complex high-risk PCI (IA-CHIP) followed by transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).
We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing simultaneous IA-CHIP and TAVR at 3 tertiary centers between January 2015 and March 2026. All patients received mechanical circulatory support with percutaneous microaxial flow pump Impella CP (Abiomed) during PCI, followed by transfemoral TAVR in the same session. Baseline demographics, procedural characteristics, and clinical outcomes were collected. The primary endpoint was in-hospital complications, including death, stroke, major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 2, 3, or 5), acute kidney injury, permanent pacemaker implantation, and vascular complications.
A total of 12 patients were included (median age, 79.5 years [IQR, 77.0-81.2]; 91.7% male; median Charlson Comorbidity Index of 7 [IQR, 5.8-9]). Coronary lesions mainly involved left main disease in 66% of cases. Advanced calcium modification was required in 50% of cases. The median aortic valve area was 0.86 cm2, and median mean gradient was 38 mm Hg. Procedural success for IA-CHIP and TAVR was 100%. There were no in-hospital deaths, strokes, or major vascular complications. Conduction disturbances requiring permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 25%. An acute kidney injury occurred in 16.7% of cases, with no requirement for dialysis. The majority of patients (91.7%) were discharged home.
A single-session strategy of IA-CHIP followed by TAVR is feasible and safe in selected patients with complex coronary artery disease and severe aortic stenosis.

title: Clinical Efficacy of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Diabetes: A Global Retrospective Study.
authors: Muhammad Hanif; Waasay H Khan; Shiva P Sah; Jai S Nagarajan; Jenish Bhandari; Stephen J Knohl; Cynthia C Taub; Andrew M Weinberg; Ankur Kalra
journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), a standard therapy for aortic stenosis, is preferred for older or high-risk patients. Various complications, including heart failure (HF), resulting in increased mortality, have been reported in the literature. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are recommended in HF, irrespective of ejection fraction; however, their role in reducing post-TAVR cardiovascular complications remains underexplored. We conducted a retrospective study to evaluate cardiovascular outcomes associated with the use of SGLT2i in post-TAVR patients.
This retrospective cohort was based on a global database of electronic health records of more than 160 million patients. After propensity-score matching, the study population included 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients divided into 2 cohorts based on their exposure to SGLT2i. Exposure to SGLT2i was defined as exposure after 1 day of TAVR.
In this study of 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients, the primary outcome of major adverse cardiovascular events and secondary outcomes, ie, cardiovascular mortality, ischemic stroke, and HF exacerbation, were significantly reduced in SGLT2i-exposed post-TAVR patients at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up. Hemorrhagic stroke was comparable at the 1-month follow-up; however, it was significantly lower in SGLT2i-exposed cohorts at the 1-year follow-up. The risk of new-onset myocardial infarction was significantly reduced at 1 month; however, it was comparable between the 2 cohorts at the 1-year follow-up. Our study also demonstrated a significant reduction in the risk of end-stage renal disease in the SGLT2i-exposed cohort at the 1-year follow-up. The periprocedural risk of acute kidney injury (within 7 days of TAVR) as well as at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up was significantly lower in the SGLT2i-exposed cohort.
In this study, post-TAVR SGLT2i use in diabetic patients was associated with reduced cardiovascular morbidity and mortality for up to 1 year.

title: Severe dynamic left-ventricular outflow-tract obstruction unmasked by transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a case report.
authors: Zongmei Gao; Minghui Yuan; Yi Li; Jingli Lu; Ruijian Li
abstract:
Relieving the fixed afterload of severe aortic stenosis can unmask a previously concealed dynamic outflow-tract obstruction.
A 69-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.65 cm2; 109/64 mmHg), mild concentric hypertrophy (septum 15 mm), and no baseline systolic anterior motion (SAM) underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The invasive peak-to-peak gradient fell from 64 to 7 mmHg, but echocardiography immediately afterwards showed new SAM and severe dynamic left-ventricular-outflow-tract (LVOT) obstruction (170/67 mmHg) with hypotension. Treatment was load-directed (volume expansion, avoidance of vasodilators and inotropes, beta-blockade), with a cardiac myosin inhibitor as an adjunct. Over 4 months the resting LVOT gradient fell to 22/13 mmHg and the provoked peak to 29 mmHg, with SAM no longer seen and preserved ejection fraction.
Recognizing this load-dependent obstruction during the procedure and restoring loading, rather than escalating inotropes, is the key lesson.

title: Association of haematologic parameters with persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children: a pilot study.
authors: Nida Gülderen Kalay Şentürk; Sevim Aslı Ehlil; Ali Karakaş; Samed Cihad Çelik; Nergis Akay; Büşra Albayrak; Hazal Cansu Çulpan; İlker Kemal Yücel; Özgür Kasapçopur; Reyhan Dedeoğlu
abstract:
Rheumatic heart disease remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity in children. Although echocardiography is central to diagnosis and staging, it does not directly reflect inflammatory processes that may contribute to ongoing valvular damage. This study aimed to evaluate the association between baseline haematologic parameters and persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children with prior acute rheumatic fever.
In this single-centre retrospective pilot study, 45 children with persistent rheumatic heart disease were classified as Stage A (n = 23), Stage B (n = 14), or Stage C (n = 8) according to the 2023 World Heart Federation echocardiographic staging framework. Baseline laboratory values obtained during acute presentation were analysed. Clinical and laboratory variables were compared across stages using non-parametric tests. Binary logistic regression identified factors associated with advanced disease (Stage B-C vs Stage A).
Markers reflecting acute inflammatory activity, including leukocyte counts and derived indices, did not differ significantly among stages. In contrast, red cell distribution width, mean platelet volume, and platelet distribution width differed significantly. In multivariable analysis, red cell distribution width, and mean platelet volume were independently associated with advanced persistent rheumatic heart disease stage, with higher values linked to increased odds of Stage B-C disease.
Red cell distribution width and mean platelet volume were associated with advanced stages of persistent paediatric rheumatic heart disease. These widely available haematologic markers may complement echocardiographic assessment. Larger prospective studies are needed to define their clinical utility.Trial registration: Not applicable (retrospective study).

title: Chest Radiotherapy Associated Cardiotoxicity: An Update.
authors: Raksheeth Agarwal; Antony Gonzalo Gonzales-Uribe; Lili Zhang
abstract:
Chest radiotherapy has improved cancer survival in various thoracic malignancies, including breast cancer, Hodgkin lymphoma, and lung cancer. However, inadvertent radiation exposure to the heart is associated with a broad spectrum of cardiovascular toxicities, collectively termed radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD). We aim to review the pathophysiology of RIHD and the current evidence for their incidence, risk factors, clinical management, and prevention strategies.
RIHD is mediated by oxidative stress, DNA damage, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and progressive fibrosis, leading to accelerated atherosclerosis, myocardial stiffening, valvular degeneration, pericardial disease, and arrhythmias. The risk, timing, and severity of cardiovascular complications are influenced by radiation dose and distribution, age at exposure, baseline cardiovascular risk, and concomitant cardiotoxic therapies. While younger patients may experience prolonged latency before clinical disease onset, older individuals and those with pre-existing cardiovascular disease often develop complications earlier, reflecting radiation-mediated acceleration of underlying pathology. This review summarizes the epidemiology, latency, clinical presentation, surveillance strategies, and management of the different forms of RIHD. It also discusses contemporary approaches to risk mitigation, including advances in radiation delivery techniques, aggressive cardiovascular risk factor modification, lifestyle interventions, and emerging pharmacologic strategies.

title: QSAR Modeling and Fragment Contribution Analysis of N-Benzyltryptamines at Human 5-HT2 Receptor Subtypes.
authors: Vladimir Đorđević; Iva Binić; Jovana Petrović; Jelena Stojanov; Žarko Mitić; Aleksandar M Veselinović
abstract: Serotonin 5-HT2 receptor agonists are returning to psychiatric drug development, but separating the three receptor subtypes pharmacologically remains difficult, and agonism at 5-HT2B carries a risk of valvular heart disease. A recent study reported affinities of 46 N-benzyltryptamines and N-benzyl-5-methoxytryptamines at all three human subtypes and analyzed them with an additive substituent model, which gave fragment coefficients of the same sign at every subtype and suggested that selectivity within this scaffold would be hard to achieve. We revisited that conclusion with non-additive models built under a protocol designed for small datasets: fifty stratified partitions with all filtering and hyperparameter tuning inside each training set, external statistics reported as distributions, response permutation on three partitions per endpoint, and partitions that withhold an entire scaffold or an entire substitution position. We repeated the analysis with two descriptor sets that share no variables and are built on different principles. Penalized linear models were predictive and transferable, whereas gradient boosting reproduced the training set exactly, and neither tree ensemble transferred to a held-out scaffold. Fragment contributions at 5-HT2A and 5-HT2C correlated at 0.25 compared with 0.77 for whole-molecule affinities, and both descriptor sets gave the same figure within 0.01. All models failed on para-substituted analogs, which distance-based applicability-domain criteria did not flag, whereas models trained without the ortho or the meta block stayed above a mean-predictor baseline. Aggregation over the whole molecule, rather than descriptor choice, conceals subtype divergence. One group drives the divergence: the N-benzyl substituent raises the predicted 5-HT2A affinity and lowers the predicted 5-HT2C affinity; excluding it raised the correlation to 0.93.

title: Association of Perioperative Colchicine Use with Morbidity and Inflammation in Heart Valve Surgery.
authors: Mehmet Burak Gulcan; Mehmet Ali Kaygın; Aycan Mutlu Yaganoglu; Ziya Yıldız; Abdulselam Karaduman; Suleyman Aycan; Ozgur Dag
abstract: Background and Objectives: Valvular heart disease (VHD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and valve replacement surgery performed under cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) with full sternotomy remains an important treatment modality. Colchicine has well-established anti-inflammatory effects in ischemic heart disease and pericardial disease, but its association with postoperative morbidity in patients undergoing valvular heart surgery has not been well studied. This study aimed to investigate the association of perioperative colchicine use with clinical morbidity and inflammatory parameters in patients undergoing valvular heart surgery with CPB. Materials and Methods: In this retrospective study, 82 patients who underwent elective on-pump valvular heart surgery through full sternotomy were divided into a control group (n = 42) who did not receive colchicine and a colchicine group (n = 40) who received oral colchicine (0.5 mg once daily) for three days before and ten days after surgery. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data, including length of hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) stay, transfusion requirements, sternal wound complication, surgical re-exploration, and inflammatory parameters on postoperative day 5 (C-reactive protein [CRP], white blood cell count, albumin, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio [PLR], and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR]), were compared between the groups. Results: Length of ICU stay was significantly shorter in the colchicine group than in the control group (4.1 ± 1.6 vs. 5.3 ± 2.4 days; p = 0.009), and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirement was significantly lower in the colchicine group (4.2 ± 2.1 vs. 6.9 ± 3.3 units; p < 0.001). Total hospital stay, erythrocyte transfusion requirement, and inflammatory parameters (CRP, white blood cell count, NLR, PLR, and albumin) did not differ significantly between the two groups (all p > 0.05). Conclusions: Perioperative colchicine was associated with a shorter ICU stay and a reduced requirement for fresh frozen plasma transfusion in patients undergoing valvular heart surgery with CPB, suggesting that colchicine may have a potential role in this surgical population. After correction for multiple comparisons, the difference in ICU length of stay was no longer statistically significant. Larger prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Seasonal Initiation of Hemodialysis: A Single-Center Experience.
authors: Derya Başak Tanburoğlu; Emrah Günay; Hatice Geçol; İbrahim Dayanan; Muhammed Emin Arslan; Gökçe Paşa
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the seasonal pattern of hemodialysis initiation in a warm/subtropical climate region (Adana) and its association with the mode of initiation, early complications, and mortality. Materials and Methods: A total of 319 patients who started chronic hemodialysis at Adana City Training and Research Hospital, Department of Nephrology, between 2022 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Chi-square/Fisher's exact and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used for seasonal comparisons. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease (coronary artery and/or valvular heart disease) were fitted for emergent initiation and for any early (30-day) complication, with a likelihood-ratio test of season as a whole; 3-month mortality (13 events) was described by season and analyzed with a season-only Firth model. Catheter dysfunction was analyzed among catheter-exposed patients, followed by sensitivity analyses. Results: A total of 58.3% of patients started dialysis emergently and 41.7% in a planned manner; only 11.3% had an arteriovenous fistula as initial vascular access. No significant seasonal differences were found in initiation type, indications, or the frequency of any early complication (161/314, 51.3%; p = 0.090). In the adjusted complication model, spring versus summer gave OR = 2.33 (95% CI: 1.23-4.41, p = 0.009; Holm-adjusted p = 0.028 across the three season contrasts), but the omnibus test of seasons was not significant (p = 0.069), and spring did not differ significantly from autumn or winter. Among catheter-exposed patients, catheter dysfunction occurred in 31.4% (22/70) in the spring and 16.5% (13/79) in the summer (p = 0.035; four-season omnibus p = 0.191); this contrast was not significant after excluding initiations from February to December 2023 (p = 0.111) or when the season was assigned at the midpoint of the risk window (p = 0.114). Season was not associated with emergent initiation (omnibus p = 0.230) or with 3-month mortality (Firth OR for spring versus summer 1.12, 95% CI: 0.28-4.48). Conclusions: Hemodialysis initiation in Adana was not associated with a winter-peak pattern in initiation counts or blood pressure. Spring initiation was associated with a higher frequency of early complications, mainly catheter dysfunction, but this exploratory single-center finding was not supported by the four-season omnibus tests and was sensitive to analytic choices, and none of the 33 seasonal omnibus tests remained significant after Holm correction. It is hypothesis-generating only and does not support a seasonal practice recommendation; confirmation in larger, multicenter, prospective studies is needed.

title: Cardiovascular Manifestations of Cystic Fibrosis.
authors: Keshav Garg; Ankit Agrawal; Ahmad Mustafa; Mohab Elnashar; Gunner Gilbert; Akiva Rosenzveig; Arnav Lakkimsetti; Elio Haroun; Aro Daniela Arockiam; Karim Hoyek; Clement Tan; Tom Kai Ming Wang
abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) has undergone a remarkable transformation from a fatal childhood disease to a chronic adult condition, with a median predicted survival now exceeding 50 years following the introduction of highly effective CFTR modulator therapy (HEMT). This demographic shift has unmasked cardiovascular complications that were previously unrecognized due to premature mortality. In a multinational propensity-matched cohort, CF conferred a 65% higher risk of major adverse cardiac events (MACEs), including myocardial infarction, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation, versus matched controls (Frost et al., HR 1.65). In a separate Canadian population-based cohort, cardiovascular disease occurred at 2.9 times the rate of the general population and at least 20 years earlier (Arya et al., RR 2.9). Cardiac involvement extends beyond the traditional paradigm of cor pulmonale. CFTR is expressed in cardiomyocytes, vascular endothelium, and smooth muscle, where its dysfunction disrupts ion homeostasis, impairs nitric oxide-dependent vasodilation, and promotes oxidative stress. Clinically, these mechanisms manifest as biventricular dysfunction detectable by strain echocardiography and cardiac MRI even when ejection fraction is preserved, diffuse myocardial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction and accelerated arterial stiffness from childhood, increased arrhythmia susceptibility, and, in a single-center cohort, an unexpectedly high prevalence of pericardial calcification (18%) on chest CT that awaits independent replication. Paradoxically, while HEMT has dramatically improved pulmonary outcomes, it introduces new cardiovascular considerations including hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity, and cross-sectional data in modulator-treated cohorts show persistent cardiac abnormalities, though whether these predate treatment or would differ without it is unknown. This review synthesizes the genetic, molecular, and clinical dimensions of cardiovascular disease in CF; distinguishes direct CFTR-mediated cardiac effects from indirect consequences of chronic lung disease; examines vascular, electrophysiological, valvular, and pericardial manifestations; and discusses management implications including CFTR modulator therapy, exercise, nutritional paradigm shifts, and transplantation considerations.

title: Experiences in the Management of Type A Aortic Dissection Following Cardiovascular Interventions: A Case Series Report.
authors: Lile He; Zhiwei Zhang; Tao Tang
abstract: Background: Cardiovascular interventions such as transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) have become standard options for high-risk patients with valvular heart disease. However, iatrogenic type A aortic dissection (AAD) remains a rare but life-threatening complication, and its optimal management is controversial. Case presentation: We present four patients who developed AAD following cardiovascular interventions at our institution between 2020 and 2024, including three after TAVR and one after TEER. Three patients underwent the Bentall procedure (each requiring removal of the pre-existing transcatheter valve, and one with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting), and one underwent aortic sinus repair with ascending aorta and total arch replacement using a frozen elephant trunk, together with removal of the previously implanted TEER clip and mitral valve replacement. One patient recovered and was discharged home, another was transferred back to the cardiology department and was discharged home with no sequelae, and two left the hospital against medical advice while still in critical condition, both of whom subsequently died-one 2 days after discharge and the other immediately upon arriving home. Conclusions: Our experience indicates that patients with cardiovascular intervention-related AAD are at particularly high risk owing to pre-existing cardiac dysfunction and deterioration of other organ functions. In such patients, emergency surgical rescue can be life-saving, and the Bentall procedure proved feasible in this selected cohort; however, surgery in this setting is more complex than in routine cases. Careful evaluation, individualized surgical planning, and meticulous perioperative management are essential to improve outcomes.

title: Mesenchymal Stromal Cells for Heart Diseases: Current Perspective and Future Directions.
authors: Miłosz Andrzej Zajączkowski; Milena Deptuła-Knioła; Małgorzata Zawrzykraj-Motylińska; Agata Kaczyńska-Miotk; Michał Pikuła; Adam Kosiński
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide and continue to impose a substantial clinical burden despite major advances in pharmacological and interventional therapies. Because the adult myocardium has limited regenerative capacity, irreversible cardiomyocyte loss frequently leads to adverse remodeling and progressive heart failure (HF). Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are among the most extensively studied cell therapies for cardiac repair because of their immunomodulatory, pro-angiogenic, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic effects, mediated predominantly through paracrine signaling. This review summarizes the current evidence for MSC-based therapy in ischemic heart disease (IHD), coronary and microvascular disorders, myocardial infarction, HF, myocarditis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and valvular heart disease (VHD). We discuss MSC sources, preclinical and clinical evidence, manufacturing and dosing, delivery routes, biomaterial-assisted transplantation, preconditioning, genetic modification, and imaging for cell tracking and treatment monitoring. Although MSC therapy has shown a favorable safety profile and regenerative potential, clinical efficacy remains variable because of limited cell survival, poor myocardial retention, and heterogeneous treatment protocols. Further optimization of manufacturing, delivery, and patient selection, together with well-designed randomized trials, is required to establish standardized protocols and support clinical translation.
